question: What is the name of the engineer who brought to light the ruins at Hampi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Colonel Colin Mackenzie**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Colonel Colin Mackenzie was the engineer who discovered the ruins of Hampi in 1800: 
 
• Mackenzie was a British engineer, antiquarian, surveyor, and cartographer who worked for the English East India Company. 
 
• Mackenzie prepared the first survey map of the site, collected manuscripts, and had watercolors painted of the monuments.
 
• He also gathered information from the priests of the Virupaksha temple and the Pampadevi shrine. 
 
• Mackenzie's work helped bring the ruins of Hampi to the attention of the world, which led to the site's preservation, study, and recognition as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Matthew Boulton (1728–1809):
 
 
• An English manufacturer and business partner of James Watt in the development of steam engines.
 
• Boulton was a key figure in the Industrial Revolution and ran the famous Soho Manufactory in Birmingham, producing metal goods, steam engines, and coins.
 
• He was also involved in the founding of the Lunar Society of Birmingham.
 
 
 
• Edward Barlow (1626–1705):
 
 
• A British naval surgeon, who worked on many ships during the 17th century.
 
• He is notable for his memoirs detailing his life and the experiences of sailors during his time, offering valuable insight into the medical practices and life at sea during the Age of Sail.
 
 
 
• James Atkinson (1774–1835):
 
 
• An English chemist, naturalist, and translator, best known for his work on scientific research and his translations of important texts.
 
• He contributed to the understanding of the chemistry of gases and also worked in the field of mineralogy.
